cost_basis: Level S3 = 64 size groups. Estimate 2004 core-min, per-level cap 4014 (2x). N-squared anchored on the medium (32 groups, ~8.4 core-h) from the STRUCK case's measured 0.24 s/step -- a real datum, not an assumption. Pure N^2 OVER-estimates because the fixed-cell flow solve does not scale with group count, so the figure is conservative. Serial RANKS=1: core-minutes == wall minutes, timeout exact. Triple ~43.9 core-h, running-total cap 5280 core-min. $2.25 DERIVED at $0.0513/core-h owner-stated -- NOT measured; the box cannot read its own billing.
_triple: THE TRIPLE WAS CHOSEN BY MEASUREMENT. The Kumar-Ramkrishna feed reconstruction was run through the actual Roache classifier on every candidate r=2 family: 12/24/48 -- the obvious cheap choice -- is DIVERGENT on m4 and m5 and would have graded those limbs NOT A RESULT. 16/32/64 classifies all-CONVERGING at a uniform observed order ~2.0. A constant r=2 also makes the comparator's rref=2.0 CORRECT rather than wrong, which is one of the three defects that made the predecessor f4f80b53 ungradeable.
_gate: m0 is DEMOTED to a calibration limb (GATE_LIMBS = [1,2,3,4,5]): beta0_OF = beta0/alpha2 fixes the Damkohler number and m0 is a monotone function of Da alone, so choosing the kernel SETS m0. m1/m2/m4/m5 are the predictive content (fractional volume-moments that do not close, so they test the feed shape); m3 tests volume conservation. Section 12.2 ruled SAME and uncapped -- QMOM and a sectional method are two discretisations of the same aggregation PBE, and the manual's Target column is that PBE's ANALYTICAL solution.
